clue.text: Write in quarters, keeping copy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: S and E are two compass quarters, south and east
a crib is a copy cribbed from someone else's work

explanation.surface: An instruction to write something in lodgings while hanging on to a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write in' looks like the definition, but IN is a piece; quarters are compass points, and a crib is a copy made by cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to engrave or set down words, a form of writing.

clue.text: Bring in a politician or split it

indicators.note: split means the word it is broken open with other letters set in the gap

parts.note: taken as written
an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between importing a politician or dividing the thing in question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' tells the solver the pronoun is broken open; the surface's 'it' looks like a link to the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To import goods is to bring them into the country from abroad.

clue.text: Lures vacillating young beginner in confident fashion

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering back and forth, so the letters of lures are shaken up
the beginner of young is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Temptations waver as a novice behaves with assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacillating' rearranges LURES to SUREL; Y is the first letter of 'young'.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is an adverb expressing certainty, speaking with confidence.

clue.text: Cook demands the right sort of oven

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
an oast is a kiln for drying hops, a sort of oven

explanation.surface: A chef insists on having the correct kind of oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST, seen in Kent, is a kiln for drying hops.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast meat is one way to cook it in the oven.

clue.text: Treasured little creature turning over in bed

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the bed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning over means the creature's name is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A beloved small animal rolls over among the bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses VOLE to LOV, which goes 'in' BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Beloved means dearly loved, held as precious.

clue.text: Arrange to invest

definitions.meaning: to set things out in order, as a verb phrase
to spend money on something, as when paying out funds

explanation.surface: An instruction to organise funds for investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay out means to set things in order, and also to spend or put money into something.

clue.text: One values a quiet person giving approval

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a praiser is someone who gives praise

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken person who approves of things is treated as worthy.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quiet comes from piano in musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraiser is someone who assesses the worth of goods, a valuer.

clue.text: Too backward to incur debt

parts.note: over means too, as in overcautious
the clue word ends in ward, and ward read backwards spells draw

explanation.surface: Someone too shy to borrow money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' is a play: its second half, WARD, read back to front gives DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw an account is to withdraw more than is in it, running into debt.

clue.text: Allow for role-playing in the gallery

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: playing suggests a game, so the letters of role are moved about

explanation.surface: A gallery permits role-play activities among its exhibits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns ROLE into OLER, set 'in' TATE, the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is to put up with or permit something.

clue.text: Left with expert may well be moved

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
able means skilled, expert

explanation.surface: Something left with a specialist might well be shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT is the nautical word for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable describes something light enough to be carried about.

clue.text: A copper ring of much interest

parts.note: a copper is a penny coin, abbreviated P
a peal is a ring of bells

explanation.surface: A policeman's telephone ring proves fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: A copper is a British penny coin, written P.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is attractiveness, the quality that draws attention.

clue.text: A way the individual can obtain drink

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
I is the single individual speaking

explanation.surface: A path by which a person might get a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, short for Street, is a common way in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white wine.

clue.text: Members of the family reveal its involvement

indicators.note: involvement suggests the letters are tangled together and rearranged

explanation.surface: Kin disclose its role in some affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' rearranges REVEAL and ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives are kin, people connected by blood or marriage.

clue.text: A tree almost all the German wanted

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone longs for nearly everything the German had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL; DER is German for the.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a deciduous tree of the birch family growing near water.

clue.text: Ruthless firm

explanation.surface: A pitiless company.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard can mean unfeeling and pitiless, or solid and unyielding to touch.

clue.text: People engaged in a welcome correspondence

indicators.note: engaged in means taking part inside something, so one piece goes within

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men means people, as in the men of a village

explanation.surface: Folk taking part in a warm exchange of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' signals insertion; correspondence here means matching, not letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence can mean agreement, matching or conformity between things.

clue.text: A flash and trendy worker set about a good man

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the other pieces surround this one

parts.note: in means fashionable
an ant is the classic crossword worker
ST stands for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A quick, fashionable labourer goes after a virtuous person.
explanation.walkthrough: IN and ANT are 'set about' ST, saint, giving IN-ST-ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, a split second.

clue.text: Bill the clerk is quite correct

parts.note: AC is account, a bill
a curate is a clerk in holy orders

explanation.surface: The office worker's invoice is spot on.
explanation.walkthrough: A clerk in holy orders is a clergyman, so a CURATE qualifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means exact, without error.

clue.text: Threaten, being green and undisciplined

indicators.note: undisciplined means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inexperienced, unruly person poses a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undisciplined' rearranges GREEN and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put at risk, imperil.

clue.text: Money the painter left inside

parts.note: a cent is a coin, money
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A painter's cash was left indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Central means in the middle, toward the core.

clue.text: Fifty to one this is material

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Betting odds of fifty to one about a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty to one' looks like betting odds; it is L and ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is a delicate openwork fabric.

clue.text: Irish guy backing alternative form of transport

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the alternative word is read backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
RY is short for railway

explanation.surface: An Irishman supports a different way of getting around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OR to RO; RY is railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Rory is a common Irish man's name.

clue.text: Book put aside

definitions.meaning: to keep back for later use

explanation.surface: A volume set apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to book in advance, and to keep something back for later.

clue.text: Divided about an Oriental king once

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the divided word goes around an

parts.note: cut means divided
taken as written
E is east, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: An Eastern king of old was split over something.
explanation.walkthrough: CUT goes 'about' AN, then E for East.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute was an eleventh-century king of England, Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Choice of the Spanish in the party

indicators.note: in tells us a piece sits within the party

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spaniard's pick within a political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: EL is Spanish for the.
explanation.definitionFit: Select as an adjective means choice, carefully picked, high quality.

clue.text: The employer of superior natural flavouring

parts.note: U means upper class, superior
sage is a herb used for flavouring

explanation.surface: A boss's taste in high-class herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the manner of employing something, its use; the clue's agent noun stretches that.

clue.text: Found one entry to criticise

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: An instruction to establish one doorway in order to find fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' means cast metal in a mould, not discover.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely.

clue.text: A little souvenir — a teeny cross

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tiny keepsake that looks like a little cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, and cross is a common word for annoyed.

clue.text: Reasons an article urges reform

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: reform means to form again, so the letters of urges are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editorial piece makes the case for change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reasons' is a verb here, not a plural noun; 'reform' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason a case is to argue it, making a logical case.

clue.text: Being in credit, take a meal by the river

parts.note: to eat is to take a meal
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone with money in the bank dines beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is a living thing, any being.

clue.text: Mistakes will be made by a renegade in time

indicators.note: in tells us the renegade goes inside time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a deserter, a renegade

explanation.surface: Errors are committed by a turncoat in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: RAT goes 'in' ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors, especially a printed list of corrections in a book.

clue.text: Respectful as always in the break

indicators.note: in tells us always sits inside the break

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone deferential at all times during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: EVER goes 'in' RENT, a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect.
